correctness.rationale: PASS: Reconstructed the prime divisor-sum lemma: sigma(t) prime forces a prime power q^e with e+1 prime, and odd e then equals 1. Since phi(n) is even, sigma(phi(n)) prime forces phi(n)=2^K; odd prime factors of n are distinct Fermat primes. Odd composite cases have >=4 nonzero binary digits but sigma(n-1) prime would force n-1 a power of two; for 4|n, n-1=3 (mod 4) implies exponent one and sigma(n-1)=n composite. Even composites must be 2∏F_j; j=0 gives n=6 excluded. For omega<=2 the remaining n=2F_j has 2^(2^j+1)+1 a power of 3. Modulo 8 forces even exponent 2h and factorization (3^h-1)(3^h+1)=2^(2^j+1) forces h=1,j=1,n=10. Prime inputs reduce precisely to the conditional Fermat/Mersenne criterion; no conjectural infinite-prime claim. Independent direct small-integer sigma/phi test through 11999 gave hits 3,5,10,17 with no contrary two-support case. Tests corroborative only.

value.rationale: PASS: Resolves the first entire composite prime-support stratum of the long-standing natural OEIS A270414 joint-divisor-sum primality question for arbitrarily large integers, rather than merely extending a finite search. Distinctive structural two-factor obstruction and conditional prime classification give a useful exact boundary; no claim about omega>=3.

final_claim: For every integer n>2 with at most two distinct prime divisors, sigma(n-1) and sigma(phi(n)) are simultaneously prime iff n=10 or n is a prime Fermat number F_j with 2^(2^j+1)-1 prime; in particular 10 is the sole composite in this support layer.
